# TAB-separated; columns as in docs/content-style.md section 6. Sections follow the lessons;
# rows under 'supporting' are not introduced by any lesson (no vocabulary items).

column12: note

column1: # --- u02.l01 ¿A qué te dedicas? (gender and articles). Also new here, rows in core.tsv: hablar, día, amigo, maestro

column12: One form for a man or a woman: el or la estudiante.
Also a title of address: el ingeniero Ruiz.
Compañero de trabajo: coworker.
(Yo) trabajo also means I work.

column1: # --- u02.l02 Uno, dos, tres (numbers 0-10, plurals). Also new here, rows in core.tsv: dos, tres

column12: Before a noun: un taco, una mesa.
Always feminine, even for a man: una persona.

column1: # --- u02.l03 ¿Cómo estás? (estar). Also new here, rows in core.tsv: estar, feliz

column12: Mexico says enojado; enfadado sounds Spanish.
Estoy aburrido: I'm bored. Es aburrido: it's boring.
Estar listo: to be ready.
Estoy mal: I'm not well. The opposite of bien.
Thirty-one and up: treinta y uno, treinta y dos...
Often shortened to el cel.
The everyday verb for sending: te mando un mensaje.

column1: # --- supporting (no lesson introduces these; usable from Unit 2 on)

column12: One word. ¿Por qué? (two words) asks why.
¿Cuál es tu número?: What's your number?
De + el always becomes del.
A + el always becomes al.
¡Ya!: now!, enough!, or done.
¿A qué te dedicas?: What do you do?
Before a masculine noun: veintiún pesos.
